tier.name: arm_neon
tier.skip_why: the no-simd variant is a deliberate no-SIMD build (-march=armv8-a+nosimd): it proves the library still works without SIMD, not that NEON agrees with the reference, and its NEON bodies compile to nothing by design
tier.why: NEON is part of the ARMv8-A baseline, so -march=armv8-a already admits it: no extra flag needed, and a build that somehow lost it would fail the registry check rather than pass quietly. The -Os and -fno-tree-vectorize variants still have NEON available, so they claim the tier too; that is how the body is checked under two different optimisation shapes

notes: User-mode emulation (qemu-aarch64) of a statically linked AArch64 Linux ELF, built by the house arm-toolchain (aarch64-none-linux-gnu). Every fact here was measured before the profile was written, because a board profile is a claim about the whole chain and the m33 cell cost a day of chasing a wrong one: `file` reports 'ELF 64-bit LSB executable, ARM aarch64, version 1 (GNU/Linux), statically linked'; the k0 KAT exits 0, i.e. bit-identical to the host verdict; no linker script, no loader and no semihosting are involved - the C runtime owns startup, so the freestanding path in kat_driver.c must stay off. That switch is keyed on __ARM_ARCH_PROFILE == 'M', not on __arm__: AArch32 Linux defines __arm__ too, and taking the bare-metal path there leaves glibc's crt1.o with an undefined `main` (measured). Coverage: LP64, the Linux userspace ABI, and the ARMv8-A SIMD baseline that -march=armv8-a implies.

variants.why: size-optimised code takes different inlining/unrolling decisions
the scalar path must stay correct when the vectoriser is off
AArch64 code must also be correct without SIMD

asserts.what: no SIMD instructions in our objects
